physics_goals.quote: a 31 kg two phase xenon detector developed to observe nuclear recoils from hypothetical weakly interacting massive dark matter particles
physics_goals.value: Observe nuclear recoils from hypothetical WIMPs in a two-phase xenon detector

summary.plain: ZEPLIN-II was a 31 kg two-phase liquid xenon dark matter detector in the Boulby mine in north-east England, operating from 2005. It measured both light and electric charge to tell dark matter from background, and set limits.
summary.technical: Two-phase (liquid/gas) xenon detector with 31 kg of xenon; first underground run of 31 live days (225 kg d after fiducial and stability cuts) gave a spin-independent minimum of 6.6e-7 pb. Successor of ZEPLIN-I, predecessor of ZEPLIN-III.
